title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate on the Requirement for Criminals of Embezzlement, Bribery, Speculation, and Other Offenses to Surrender and Confess Within a Prescribed Time Limit
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate

Notice on the Requirement for Criminals of Embezzlement, Bribery, Speculation, and Other Offenses to Surrender and Confess Within a Specified Time Limit

Fa (Yan) Fa [1989] No. 21

Resolutely punishing corruption and waging a struggle against serious criminal activities in the economic sphere such as embezzlement, bribery, and speculation is an important task established by the Fourth Plenary Session of the Thirteenth Central Committee of the Communist Party of China, and a matter of common concern to the people. Severe criminal economic activities must be severely cracked down upon. In investigating and handling such criminal cases, we must adhere to the principles of taking facts as the basis, taking law as the criterion, and equality of all before the law, and resolutely implement the policy of combining punishment with leniency, leniency for those who confess, and severity for those who resist. Anyone who violates the criminal law and constitutes a crime shall be pursued for liability; anyone who voluntarily surrenders, confesses, or performs meritorious service within the specified time limit shall be dealt with leniently. In order to give criminals an opportunity to repent and reform, and to severely punish those who refuse to repent, based on the recommendations of the meeting of the Political Bureau of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China held on July 27 and 28, 1989, and relevant legal provisions, the following notice is hereby issued:

1. State functionaries who commit the crimes of embezzlement, bribery, or speculation, and the directly responsible supervisors and other directly responsible persons of enterprises, institutions, state organs, or organizations that commit the crimes of speculation or bribery, must, from the date of promulgation of this notice until October 31, 1989, voluntarily surrender to the procuratorial organs, public security organs, people's courts, or other relevant departments or their own units, confess their criminal facts, and seek lenient treatment.

2. Within the above-mentioned time limit, those who voluntarily surrender and actively return ill-gotten gains, or who have performed meritorious service by reporting others, shall be dealt with leniently in accordance with the provisions of Articles 63 and 59 of the Criminal Law. Among them, those whose crimes are especially serious and who are punishable by death according to law may be given a lighter or mitigated punishment and not sentenced to death; those whose crimes are relatively serious and who are punishable by heavy punishment according to law may be given a lighter or mitigated punishment or exempted from punishment; those whose crimes are relatively minor and who are punishable by light punishment according to law may be given a mitigated punishment or exempted from punishment.

Those who, after being subjected to compulsory measures, confess all their crimes and actively return ill-gotten gains, or who have performed meritorious service by reporting others, shall be given lenient treatment at the discretion of the court, with reference to the preceding paragraph.

3. Those who, within the specified time limit, refuse to voluntarily surrender and confess their problems; destroy evidence or transfer illicit money and goods; collude with each other to form a pact of mutual protection; or flee out of fear of punishment and refuse to surrender, shall be severely punished according to law.

4. All persons who have knowledge or understanding of criminal situations have the obligation to report or disclose them to judicial organs or relevant departments. Persons who make reports or disclosures shall be protected according to law. Persons who have made meritorious contributions through reports or disclosures shall be rewarded.

Those who obstruct, threaten, or retaliate against law enforcement personnel or persons who report, disclose, or testify shall be severely punished in accordance with the provisions of Article 157 of the Criminal Law (crime of obstructing public service) or Article 146 (crime of retaliation and framing).

Those who seize the opportunity to fabricate facts to frame or falsely accuse others shall be severely punished in accordance with the provisions of Article 138 of the Criminal Law (crime of false accusation and framing).

5. It is strictly forbidden to plead for, protect, or screen offenders of illegal or criminal acts through favoritism. Those who harbor or conceal criminals shall be severely punished in accordance with the provisions of Article 162 of the Criminal Law (crime of harboring or concealing criminals). Those who conceal or destroy evidence of crimes for criminals, or who provide or fabricate false evidence, shall be severely punished in accordance with the provisions of Article 148 of the Criminal Law (crime of perjury).

6. Other economic criminals not specified in Article 1 of this notice who voluntarily surrender, confess, or perform meritorious service by reporting others within the time limit specified in this notice shall also be subject to the provisions of Article 2 of this notice.

7. After the promulgation of this notice, in cases of embezzlement, bribery, speculation, and other economic crimes currently being handled, where criminals have circumstances of voluntary surrender, confession, or meritorious service by reporting others, the provisions of Article 2 of this notice shall apply.

August 15, 1989

Attachment: Relevant Legal Provisions

I. Legal Provisions on Lenient Treatment

Article 63 of the Criminal Law: Those who voluntarily surrender after committing a crime may be given a lighter punishment. Among them, those whose crimes are relatively minor may be given a mitigated punishment or exempted from punishment; those whose crimes are relatively serious, if they have performed meritorious service, may also be given a mitigated punishment or exempted from punishment.

Article 59 of the Criminal Law: Where a criminal has circumstances for mitigated punishment provided in this Law, the punishment shall be imposed below the statutory punishment.

Where a criminal does not have circumstances for mitigated punishment provided in this Law, but if, based on the specific circumstances of the case, imposing the minimum statutory punishment is still too harsh, with the decision of the Adjudication Committee of the People's Court, the punishment may also be imposed below the statutory punishment.

Article 101 of the Criminal Procedure Law: Where, according to the provisions of the Criminal Law, it is not necessary to impose punishment or where exemption from punishment may be granted, the People's Procuratorate may decide not to initiate prosecution.

II. Provisions on the Crime of Obstructing Public Service, the Crime of Retaliation and Framing, and Other Crimes

Crime of Obstructing Public Service:

Article 157 of the Criminal Law: Those who obstruct a state functionary from performing his duties according to law by means of violence or threat, or who refuse to execute a judgment or order that has been legally effective of a People's Court, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years, criminal detention, a fine, or deprivation of political rights.

Crime of Retaliation and Framing:

Article 146 of the Criminal Law: Where a state functionary abuses his power or uses public office for private gain to retaliate against or frame a complainant, appellant, or critic, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than two years or criminal detention; if the circumstances are serious, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than two years and not more than seven years.

Crime of False Accusation and Framing:

Article 138 of the Criminal Law: It is strictly forbidden to accuse or frame cadres or the masses by any method or means. Whoever fabricates facts to falsely accuse or frame others (including criminals) shall be given criminal sanctions with reference to the nature, circumstances, consequences, and sentencing standards of the crime for which he has framed others. Where a state functionary commits the crime of false accusation, he shall be given a heavier punishment.

Where there is no intentional false accusation but rather a mistaken accusation or a report that proves inaccurate, the provisions of the preceding paragraph shall not apply.

Crime of Harboring or Concealing Criminals, Crime of Protecting Criminals:

Article 162 of the Criminal Law: Whoever harbors a counter-revolutionary or makes false testimony to protect a counter-revolutionary shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years, criminal detention, or public surveillance; if the circumstances are serious, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years and not more than ten years.

Whoever harbors other criminals or makes false testimony to protect them shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than two years, criminal detention, or public surveillance; if the circumstances are serious, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than two years and not more than seven years.

Crime of Perjury:

Article 148 of the Criminal Law: During investigation or trial proceedings, where a witness, expert evaluator, record keeper, or translator intentionally makes a false statement, evaluation, record, or translation concerning material circumstances of a case, with the intent to frame others or conceal evidence of crime, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than two years or criminal detention; if the circumstances are serious, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than two years and not more than seven years.
